obligation: CERCLA release notice to the National Response Center
trigger: Release of a hazardous substance at or above its RQ in any 24-hour period (chlorine 10 lb; sodium hypochlorite 100 lb; sodium hydroxide 1,000 lb)
deadline: Immediately on knowledge of the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - any plant, branch, or terminal; not triggered in the exercise scenario (SIS tripped the reactor; no release)
notifying_entity: Person in charge at the facility (shift superintendent)
clock_starts: Knowledge of the release (not the cyber declaration)

obligation: EPCRA emergency release notice (immediate)
trigger: Release of an extremely hazardous substance or CERCLA hazardous substance at or above its RQ with potential offsite exposure (chlorine is both)
deadline: Immediately
notify: Community emergency coordinator for the LEPC and the SERC of each state likely to be affected

obligation: EPCRA written follow-up notice
trigger: After an immediate EPCRA notice (not for releases in transportation, 355.40(c))
deadline: As soon as practicable after the release

obligation: RMP community and responder notification (responding source)
trigger: Accidental release from the Plant C1 chlorine process
deadline: Timely data and information on the release as soon as it occurs; community notification system activated
notify: County fire rescue, emergency management, and the public in the affected area

obligation: RMP incident investigation
trigger: Incident that resulted in, or could reasonably have resulted in, a catastrophic release. An unauthorized change to a chlorine feed setpoint and reactor alarm limits meets this test even though the SIS tripped
deadline: Start as promptly as possible and no later than 48 hours after the incident
notify: Internal (investigation team including a person knowledgeable in the process)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - triggered in the exercise scenario
clock_starts: The incident (setpoint change), not the cyber declaration

obligation: RMP five-year accident history correction
trigger: Accidental release from a covered process meeting the 68.42 criteria (deaths, injuries, or significant property damage on site, or known offsite deaths, injuries, evacuations, sheltering in place, property damage, or environmental damage)
deadline: Within 6 months of the release or by the next RMP update under 68.190, whichever is earlier

obligation: RMP public meeting after an accident with offsite impacts
trigger: RMP reportable accident with known offsite impacts (68.42(a))
deadline: Within 90 days of the accident

obligation: OSHA report of a work-related fatality
trigger: Work-related fatality
deadline: Within 8 hours

obligation: OSHA report of in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye
trigger: Work-related in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye
deadline: Within 24 hours

obligation: Coast Guard report of an actual or threatened cyber incident
trigger: Evidence of an actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering Terminal T1 (in the scenario, probing of the tank gauging network from the compromised gateway)
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Captain of the Port
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Terminal T1; triggered in the exercise scenario
owner: Distribution Cybersecurity Officer (CySO) for Terminal T1

obligation: MTSA report of suspicious activity or breach of security
trigger: Activities that may result in a transportation security incident, or a breach of security, at Terminal T1
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Terminal T1; counsel and the FSO decide whether the probe is a breach of security

obligation: MTSA report of a transportation security incident
trigger: A transportation security incident at Terminal T1
deadline: Without delay; then follow the Facility Security Plan

obligation: Reportable cyber incident report to the NRC (fallback)
trigger: Reportable cyber incident not already reported to the Coast Guard under 6.16-1
deadline: Without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if the 6.16-1 report was not made
clock_starts: Determination that the incident is reportable
owner: Distribution Cybersecurity Officer (CySO) for Terminal T1

obligation: CySO records the reportable cyber incident and reports to the owner
trigger: Any reportable cyber incident at Terminal T1
deadline: Record kept at least 2 years (105.225)
notify: Distribution president (owner or operator) and the FSO
owner: Distribution Cybersecurity Officer (CySO) for Terminal T1

obligation: DOT immediate telephone report of a hazmat incident
trigger: During transportation (including loading, unloading, and temporary storage): death, hospitalization, public evacuation of 1 hour or more, major artery closed 1 hour or more, or a continuing danger to life
deadline: As soon as practical and no later than 12 hours after the occurrence
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - conditional (each division when in physical possession)
notifying_entity: Person in physical possession (driver, rack operator) through dispatch or the site
owner: Hazmat Transport Vice President of Safety and Compliance

obligation: DOT written hazmat incident report (Form F 5800.1)
trigger: Any 171.15 incident or an unintentional release in transportation
deadline: Within 30 days of discovery
owner: Hazmat Transport Vice President of Safety and Compliance

obligation: Keep the emergency response number monitored
trigger: Any group hazmat shipment in transportation while systems are down
deadline: Continuous; the number must be monitored at all times and the responder must have immediate access to response information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all divisions; the ERC runs from its backup site with offline SDS if SYS-G7 is affected

obligation: Notify employees when security plan elements must be implemented
trigger: Heightened threat to hazmat shipments (for example dispatch or shipping paper systems compromised)
deadline: When the elements must be implemented (per each plan)
notify: Drivers, dispatchers, rack and shipping staff
notifying_entity: Each division under its security plan

obligation: ELD malfunction notice from drivers
trigger: ELD malfunction (for example a telematics vendor outage)
deadline: Within 24 hours; drivers keep paper logs and reconstruct the prior 7 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - conditional; not triggered in the scenario (ELDs unaffected)
owner: Hazmat Transport Director of Fleet Technology

obligation: ELD repair or extension request
trigger: Carrier learns of an ELD malfunction
deadline: Correct within 8 days; request an extension within 5 days after the driver notice if needed
notify: FMCSA Division Administrator for the state of the principal place of business
clock_starts: Driver notice or discovery, whichever is first
owner: Hazmat Transport Director of Fleet Technology

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)

obligation: Disclosure committee escalation
trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration

obligation: Florida notice to affected individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (in the scenario, HR and driver qualification exports, about 1,900 Florida residents)
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach (15-day extension for good cause, individual notice only)
notifying_entity: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. (employer of record for each division)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the group (inbound)
trigger: A vendor maintaining personal information for the group (HR and payroll SaaS, driver records SaaS) has a breach
deadline: Within 10 days after the vendor determines the breach

obligation: Other states: notice to affected individuals
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (about 5,500 people in 40 other states in the scenario)
deadline: Varies by state; counsel applies each state law in parallel with Florida

obligation: Other states: regulator notices
citation: State breach notification statutes (attorney general or other regulator where required)
trigger: Thresholds vary by state
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorneys general or other designated regulators

obligation: Voluntary report to the FBI and CISA
citation: Voluntary; POL-03 (supports OFAC mitigation if a payment is considered)
trigger: Confirmed intrusion into OT or ransomware
deadline: Within 24 hours (group target)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR Chapter V
trigger: Any consideration of a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC (if a sanctions nexus is suspected); counsel

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (call the breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - proposed only; final rule not published as of 2026-10-05

obligation: CFATS significant security incident report (RBPS 15)
trigger: Significant security incident at a covered facility
deadline: Not enforceable while CFATS authority is lapsed
applies_at_this_tier: No - CFATS authority expired 2023-07-28; voluntary FBI and CISA report used instead

obligation: Water utility customers: delivery impact notice
trigger: Automatic replenishment or Plant C1 hypochlorite supply interrupted
deadline: Within 4 hours of the decision to switch to manual replenishment (contract term)
notify: About 640 utility customers on the managed inventory service
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - triggered in the scenario (ERP order release stopped)
clock_starts: Decision to switch to manual replenishment

obligation: Managed inventory customers: security incident notice
citation: Managed inventory service agreements (contract; 72-hour term for the 12 largest customers)
trigger: Security incident affecting customer data or the managed inventory platform
deadline: Within 72 hours for the 12 largest customers; otherwise without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - conditional (not triggered: SYS-D3 not compromised in the scenario)
clock_starts: Confirmation that customer data or SYS-D3 was affected

obligation: Hazmat Transport shippers: load delay notice
citation: Carrier contracts with about 1,400 third-party shippers
trigger: Dispatch or shipping papers unavailable
deadline: Same day

obligation: Integrator or OEM notice to the group (inbound)
citation: Group security addendum (POL-01 4.8); 33 CFR 101.650(f)(2) for Terminal T1 vendors
trigger: Integrator learns its credentials, staff, or tools are compromised (in the scenario, the stolen integrator credential)
deadline: Without delay
notify: Group SOC and the Terminal T1 CySO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendor duty; 6 of 14 integrator contracts lack the term (POAM-022)

obligation: Board risk committee briefing
trigger: Severity 1 incident
deadline: Within 24 hours of declaration, then daily during response
